rules.title: PDSPrj is ZIP-style container
rules.rule: .pdsprj files begin with PK and contain internal project files such as PROJECT.XML, ROOT.DSN, ROOT.CDB, and SCRIPTS/PWRRAILS.DAT.

rules.title: ROOT.DSN controls visual object existence
rules.rule: Components visible in ROOT.DSN appear in Proteus even if ROOT.CDB is missing entries; CDB-only components do not create visible schematic objects.

rules.title: ROOT.CDB controls resistor values and references
rules.rule: For existing resistors, ROOT.CDB is authoritative for value and reference designator. ROOT.DSN display metadata can be normalized from ROOT.CDB on open/save.

rules.title: Terminal labels live in ROOT.DSN
rules.rule: INPUT, OUTPUT, POWER, and GROUND terminal objects and labels are stored in ROOT.DSN. Terminal-only changes do not alter ROOT.CDB.

rules.title: Topology is ROOT.DSN-controlled
rules.rule: Series/parallel/ladder topology changes are represented in ROOT.DSN through terminal labels, wire stubs, and object layout. ROOT.CDB can remain identical across different topologies with the same component refs/values.

rules.title: ROOT.CDB must exist
rules.rule: Removing ROOT.CDB entirely causes fatal Proteus/ISIS failure. A generator must include ROOT.CDB, even if minimal.

rules.title: PWRRAILS.DAT unchanged in early terminal/passive tests
rules.rule: Visible VCC/GND terminals and resistor networks did not modify SCRIPTS/PWRRAILS.DAT. For early generator versions, copy this file unchanged from a template.

rules.title: V9 resistor generator uses linked endpoint groups
rules.rule: For generated resistor networks, emit matching input/output terminal records, a resistor visual record, and two short-wire records with consistent link suffixes and only one final terminator at the end of the object stream.

rules.title: V9 resistor generation uses E001 as base
rules.rule: Use the blank E001 project as the .pdsprj container base for resistor generation. Donor projects may provide byte-record templates, but generated outputs replace ROOT.CDB and ROOT.DSN and copy PROJECT.XML/PWRRAILS from E001.

rules.title: Power and ground endpoint terminals are label-width constrained
rules.rule: For the locked resistor V9 method, use two-character labels such as V0 and G0. Power bridge labels and resistor terminal labels remain two-character; $TERGROUND is safe as a right endpoint replacement for $TEROUTPUT.

rules.title: Resistor visual rotation field
rules.rule: In the V9 resistor visual record, the four bytes after the final model placement x/y pair store rotation as a signed tenths-of-degrees value in the low 16 bits. 0 is horizontal; -900 is vertical down. Vertical generation must rotate terminal/wire endpoint positions along the same axis.

rules.title: Standalone visual wires are disabled in production resistor generation
evidence: user reported VGDVC.dll errors on parallel-and-later visual-wire cases
rules.rule: Do not emit standalone layout.visual_wires in the production resistor generator. Parse and record them as skipped until a Proteus-created donor establishes VGDVC-safe standalone wire records.

rules.title: Power nodes use donor-derived output bridge
rules.rule: The main resistor generator must emit one donor-derived $TERPOWER -> $TEROUTPUT(V0) bridge for the power node. Powered resistor endpoints stay ordinary $TERINPUT(V0) terminals so same-name terminal topology connects them to the bridge.

rules.title: Dense resistor layouts are stretched before generation
evidence: user reported overlapped generated resistor circuits
rules.rule: Treat manual component coordinates as placement hints. If repeated x/y positions are closer than the safe V9 grid, stretch them before emitting ROOT.DSN so terminal records, short wires, and resistor visual bodies do not overlap. The current production safe grid is 2540000 internal units on both x and y.

rules.title: Resistor generator is locked as main for current scope
rules.rule: Use src/proteusgen/resistor_v9.py as the main resistor generator. Do not reintroduce direct $TERPOWER resistor endpoints or standalone production visual wires. New component work starts with capacitor support.

rules.title: Capacitor work stays temporary until Proteus accepts guarded diagnostics
rules.rule: Free capacitor multi-component generation using CAP_T01 visual cores and cap3-derived CDB/object expansion is user-accepted. V10 confirms the manual donor outputs-first order opens for exact, translated, renamed, and three-cap terminal-attached cases. V11 confirms the same method scales to 6C and 21C terminal-label networks. Keep the capacitor generator temporary until the V13 wider-spacing requested 15 capacitor-network pack with real power/ground terminals is Proteus accepted.

rules.title: Manual two-terminal-cap donor uses outputs-first object order
rules.rule: The user-made two-terminal-capacitor donor object chunk is ordered as: header, all $TEROUTPUT records, then each $TERINPUT/CAPACITOR/left-wire/right-wire group. Every non-final right-wire record is 49 bytes, omitting the usual trailing terminator byte; the final right-wire record is 50 bytes and ends with FF.

rules.title: Mixed resistor/capacitor passive generation is locked
rules.rule: Use src/proteusgen/mixed_passive.py as the main mixed resistor/capacitor generator for the current scope. The locked object stream order is header, one power bridge, capacitor output array, capacitor groups, resistor input array, resistor output array, separator, resistor groups. Use a 2540000 internal-unit safe grid and shift duplicate positions so components are not generated on top of each other.

rules.title: Inductor generation requires controlled donors before coding
evidence: BIG06 inductor/source empty-CDB trial opened/saved/simulated but is not a controlled donor
rules.rule: Do not infer inductor object bytes from unrelated corpus scans. Use the user-created E001-based inductor donors as record templates, then test the same terminal-first method used for resistor/capacitor generation.

rules.title: Inductor V1 donor object order
rules.rule: The first inductor V1 generator used the user-created three-terminal-inductor donor order, but all V1 generated outputs caused VGDVC.dll errors. Do not reuse V1 as positive evidence. Initial diff against the known-good two-terminal donor shows the first mutation is the terminal/component link suffix sequence; V2 must preserve donor REALIND link suffix bytes before testing further mutations.

rules.title: Inductor V2 starts with exact donor controls
rules.rule: Exact inductor donor repacks, exact donor object chunks inserted into E001, suffix-preserved single-inductor mutation, renamed/translated single-inductor mutation, and exact power/ground donor insertion work in Proteus 8.13. The generated three-inductor V2 T7 case failed, so multi-inductor generation must not be promoted from V2.

rules.title: Inductor multi-generation needs per-index diagnostics
rules.rule: For multi-inductor generation, preserve the REALIND visual record for each donor index rather than selecting only by visible value length. V3 confirms exact per-index rebuild, text mutation with donor geometry, rigid donor-geometry translation, renamed rigid translation, and formula-coordinate rebuild with per-index REALIND templates all open in Proteus 8.13.

rules.title: Inductor power/ground generation remains lock-candidate
rules.rule: Do not prepend the generic passive $TERPOWER -> $TEROUTPUT(V0) bridge before generated REALIND groups. V4 T1, T2, T3, and T5 opened partially then reported bad object record; V4 T4 gave an ISIS.dll error. The visible result showed a detached power bridge plus a separate V0 input label, so generic passive bridge ordering is rejected for inductors.

rules.title: Inductor power/ground must preserve donor04 order
rules.rule: The accepted inductor_04 power/ground donor order is input terminal, REALIND, trimmed left wire, power terminal, output terminal, bridge wire, ground terminal, final ground wire. V5 confirms exact donor04 chunk controls plus small ref/value/internal-node mutations work when preserving this order.

rules.title: Inductor promotion was premature and is demoted to temporary
rules.rule: Do not treat src/proteusgen/inductor.py or the generate-inductors CLI as main/locked. The current inductor implementation is copied to tools/proteus_generation/2026-06-01/inductor_temp_from_premature_main. The V6 6/21, V7 requested-15, and R/C/L V1 packs all failed in Proteus, so inductor promotion is blocked until new larger inductor donor evidence is supplied.

rules.title: Inductor donor03 does not extrapolate past three components
rules.rule: The accepted three-inductor V3 donor can be used only within its known three-slot scope. Repeating donor suffixes or extending suffixes from the third donor slot failed for six and twenty-one inductor generated projects. Do not generate larger inductor networks until a Proteus-created six-or-more-inductor donor provides the real object order and link/suffix pattern.

rules.title: Six-inductor donor uses sequential groups
rules.rule: The six-inductor donor object chunk is ordered as six repeated $TERINPUT/$TEROUTPUT/REALIND/left-wire/right-wire groups, not as the three-inductor donor order. The capacitor-family trim rule does apply: non-final right-wire records are 49 bytes and the final right-wire is 50 bytes. User testing confirmed V8 exact controls, six/21 generated sequential cases, the outputs-first probe, and the sequential power/ground bridge probe worked; prefer donor05 sequential order for the next inductor topology packs.

rules.title: Requested inductor topology packs stay temporary until user-opened
rules.rule: Generate requested multi-inductor V0/G0 topology packs from the accepted donor05 sequential method and donor-derived V0 bridge. Do not promote inductor code to main until the requested 15 inductor circuits and the later R/C/L mixed circuits are user-accepted.

rules.title: R/C/L mixed generation uses accepted V8 inductors
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V2 method
rules.rule: Do not reuse the failed R/C/L V1 inductor composition or the V2 R/C-then-L-last object order. V3 confirms capacitor+inductor can work when the capacitor-family block precedes the inductor block or uses joined outputs-first ordering. V5 confirms free R/L/C component records can coexist and be inserted into E001. V6 shows terminal-attached C and L work around a free resistor. V7 T02-T07 show a terminal-attached resistor can coexist with free L/C when the resistor block is placed last/final. V8 shows this does not extend to terminal C/L plus final R: only the free L/C control T01 worked, and no-power all-terminal T02 failed. V9 then showed all generated minimal terminal R+L order/index/suffix variants failed. Stop generated guessing at this boundary and require a Proteus-created terminal-attached resistor plus terminal-attached inductor donor before producing more R/C/L topology packs.

rules.title: Manual RLC donor is a family-order donor, not a topology donor
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V5 method
rules.rule: The user-supplied rlc_manual_donor object chunk contains free component records in L1, R1, C1 order with matching ROOT.CDB entries, but contains no $TERINPUT, $TEROUTPUT, $TERPOWER, $TERGROUND, or WIRE records. User testing confirmed V5 T01-T04 donor controls work, so this donor is valid evidence for free component coexistence, DSN header compatibility, and CDB metadata. It is not evidence for generated terminal topology: V5 T05-T10 all failed.

rules.title: RLC terminal topology must be isolated by family
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V6 method
rules.rule: V6 identifies the family boundary: terminal-attached L with free R/C works, terminal-attached C with free L/R works, terminal-attached C+L with free R works in disconnected and connected forms, but terminal-attached R fails in every tested combination containing an inductor. Do not generate R/C/L topologies with the current V9 resistor terminal record until resistor-specific diagnostics pass.

rules.title: RLC terminal resistor suffix and order must be tested before topology generation
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V7 method
rules.rule: V7 T02-T07 show terminal R can coexist with free L/C if free L/C records are first and the resistor terminal block is final. The specific ordinal/index/suffix policy was not the deciding factor because all tested variants T02-T07 worked. V8 shows that this rule does not solve all-terminal R/C/L: only T01 worked, and T02 without power/ground failed. Do not infer full all-terminal R/C/L support from the V7 free-L/C result.

rules.title: RLC terminal resistor final ordering is positive only for free L/C scope
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V7/V8 method
rules.rule: When a project contains free capacitor and inductor donor records, a terminal-attached resistor works if its complete terminal/resistor/wire block is the final object block. This is not sufficient when the inductor is terminal-attached: V8 T02 failed without power/ground. Do not proceed to larger R/C/L topologies until a minimal terminal R plus terminal L case works or a manual donor reveals the native Proteus R/L object order.

rules.title: RLC active blocker is terminal resistor plus terminal inductor
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V8/V9 method
rules.rule: The first failing condition is not power/ground, shared terminal labels, or large component count. V8 T02 failed with disconnected labels and no power/ground. Existing positive evidence covers terminal C+L with free R and terminal R with free L/C. V9 directly tested minimal terminal R+L order, index, and suffix hypotheses; the user reported none worked. Do not generate larger mixed R/C/L circuits until a clean Proteus-created terminal R+L donor is analyzed.

rules.title: Manual terminal R+L donor is required
rules.rule: The corpus includes Proteus-created terminal R+L donors. The disconnected donor is the primary mutation template: its native object order is header, both inputs, L output+REALIND+wires, then R output+RESISTOR+wires. User testing confirmed V10 donor controls, donor-native mutation, connected labels, translation, and V0/G0 R+L all work. Larger mixed R/C/L still requires V11 6/21 and requested-15 acceptance before promotion.

rules.title: Native terminal R+L order uses inputs-first mixed groups
rules.rule: For a Proteus-created disconnected terminal R+L project, ROOT.DSN object data is not normal resistor V9 order and not inductor sequential group order. It is header, two $TERINPUT records, then the inductor's $TEROUTPUT/REALIND/left-wire/right-wire group, then the resistor's $TEROUTPUT/boundary-byte/RESISTOR/left-wire/right-wire group. V10 confirms this native order is safe for single-pair mutation, connected labels, coordinate translation, and V0/G0 R+L.

rules.title: Scaled RCL uses repeated native R/L pairs
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V11 method
rules.rule: V11's scaled object order was not enough for simulation. It emitted one donor-derived V0 bridge, the accepted capacitor output/group block, then repeated native R/L pair blocks, but it reused per-family DSN component IDs and wrote ROOT.CDB in source order. Proteus netlist compilation reported duplicate part references and duplicate generated X00000001 handles. Do not promote or reuse V11 without global component identity and CDB ordering fixes.

rules.title: Mixed RCL simulation needs global component IDs
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V12 method
rules.rule: For mixed terminal R/C/L projects, visible component refs are not enough. The DSN component identity field used by CAPACITOR, REALIND, and RESISTOR records must be globally unique across families, and ROOT.CDB component tables must use the same IDs in DSN object-emission order. V12 fixed the single 1C+1L+1R cases such as simple loop and basic divider, but user testing reported that remaining cases with additional resistor, capacitor, or inductor components still failed. Therefore global IDs and object-order CDB are necessary but not sufficient for scaled R/C/L.

rules.title: Scaled RCL may require all R/L inputs before R/L bodies
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V13 method
rules.rule: The one-pair R+L donor proves only that both R/L input terminals precede that pair's output/component bodies. V12 repeated complete native L/R pair blocks, placing pair 2 inputs after pair 1 bodies; user testing then showed only single 1C+1L+1R cases worked. V13 kept global IDs and CDB object-order alignment, and emitted every R/L input terminal first across all native pairs before L/R bodies, but user feedback still reported multi-component cases failed. Do not promote V13.

rules.title: Scaled RCL donor repeats complete C/L/R units
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V14 method
rules.rule: The supplied 4x mixed R/C/L donor does not use pooled capacitor blocks or pooled R/L input arrays. Its ROOT.DSN object data is one V0 power bridge followed by four complete units: C output, C input+CAPACITOR+wires, L input, R input, L $TERGROUND+REALIND+wires, then R output+RESISTOR+wires. Suffixes advance by 0x07d6, equal to the 2006-byte non-final unit length, and the final unit's R right-wire record is 51 bytes with the final FF terminator. V14 T00 and T00B proved that exact donor repack and donor chunk+CDB insertion into E001 are valid. Every generated V14 case after that failed with Bad Object Record/corrupt pink wires, so the repeated-unit donor shape is real but V14's mutation strategy is not safe.

rules.title: Mixed RCL resistor record offsets depend on visible value length
rules.rule: The RESISTOR record inside the supplied mixed R/C/L donor has visible value '10k' with length 3. As a result, the component identity field is at value_offset+252, observed as byte offset 325 for the donor record, and the pin-link suffix fields start at value_offset+265 and value_offset+269. Fixed resistor-only V9 offsets are unsafe for mixed-family resistor records when the visible value length changes.

rules.title: RCL Bad Object Record boundary is generated mutation
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V15 method
rules.rule: Because V14 T00 and T00B worked, the exact 4x donor object chunk, donor CDB, and E001 transplant path are valid. V15 user testing showed full 4x donor terminal-label mutations T01-T03 worked, while the generated-body case T04 failed. Exact first-unit shortening with a 50-byte final right-wire record failed in T05/T06, but the 51-byte final right-wire variant T07 worked. Therefore terminal labels are safe, generated body/coordinate mutation was the active corruption boundary, and shortened RCL streams must preserve the donor's extra final FF terminator byte.

rules.title: Mixed RCL wire coordinates are marker-relative
rules.rule: Do not patch mixed RCL WIRE coordinates at a fixed byte offset. In the 4x RCL donor, capacitor and inductor wire records contain the WIRE marker at byte 24 and coordinates at byte 33, but resistor wire records contain the WIRE marker at byte 25 and coordinates at byte 34. Patch WIRE coordinates at marker_position + 9. V14 used byte 33 for all wires, corrupting resistor wire records and producing Bad Object Record/pink-wire rendering. V16 user testing confirmed this marker-relative rule works for 1x, 2x, 3x, 4x, 6x, 7x, and 21x full R/C/L repeated-unit outputs.

rules.title: Mixed RCL component removal stays diagnostic
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V17 method
rules.rule: Whole C/L/R subgroups can be removed from accepted V16 repeated units to form RC, LC, RL, and C-only branches. V17 keeps donor subgroup order, patches WIRE coordinates at marker_position + 9, and gives the final kept subgroup a valid final FF wire terminator. User testing confirmed the RC, LC, RL, C-only, and requested 3R/4C/1L cases worked, so this method is valid for the temporary V18 final-topology pack.

rules.title: Mixed RCL final topology pack uses V17 subgroup-removal units
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V18 method
rules.rule: V18 correctly reused accepted V17 full/removal groups, E001 base, V0 bridge, G0 endpoints, marker-relative WIRE coordinate patching, and global component IDs, but its T02 21-component case is invalid as a final acceptance case because it emitted seven independent V0-to-G0 RCL branches. A 21-component test must follow the accepted 21-circuit topology, not merely contain 21 components. Do not promote V18 as final.

rules.title: Correct 21 circuit topology has three seven-component paths
rules.rule: The corrected 21-component mixed R/C/L circuit must follow the earlier accepted 21R/21RC rule: one seven-component series string from V0 to M0, a second seven-component series string from V0 to M0, and a third seven-component series string from M0 to G0. V19 implements this with accepted V17 groups arranged as RCL+RC+LC, RCL+RL+RC, and RCL+LC+RL, giving exactly 7 resistors, 7 capacitors, and 7 inductors. User testing confirmed this corrected 21 circuit worked.

rules.title: Mixed RCL generator is locked as main for current scope
rules.rule: Use src/proteusgen/mixed_rcl.py as the main mixed resistor/capacitor/inductor generator for the current scope. It emits E001-based projects using the accepted 4x RCL donor schema, marker-relative WIRE coordinate patching, global component IDs, ROOT.CDB in object-emission ID order, and accepted whole-subgroup modes RCL, RC, LC, RL, C, R, and L. The locked examples include the 6-component case, corrected 21-rule topology, and 15 requested topologies.

rules.title: Mixed RCL value overrides must keep donor value length
rules.rule: When overriding visible values in src/proteusgen/mixed_rcl.py, keep the existing donor value field length. Current safe overrides are exactly three ASCII characters for resistors, capacitors, and inductors. Use compact Proteus text such as 10R for 10 ohm, 50R for 50 ohm, 4u7 for 4.7 uF, 10u for 10 uF, and 10m for 10 mH. A two-character resistor value such as 10 corrupts the mixed-family resistor record because downstream fields shift.

rules.title: DC voltage source-net diagnostics use ordinary terminals
rules.rule: The user-made combined DC-voltage plus six-component R/C/L donor contains no $TERPOWER and no $TERGROUND records. Its source-driven nets use ordinary terminal labels: DV for the DC-voltage positive net and D0 for the negative net. V5 user testing confirmed the manual donor transplant, manual label-only mutation, and generated source-net R/C/L body with no source object worked. The generated VSOURCE-first and VSOURCE-last cases both failed with VGC/VG... dll, so the source-net conversion is accepted as a direction but generated VSOURCE insertion remains unresolved.

rules.title: DC voltage source block must preserve donor source bytes
rules.rule: After V5 isolated the failure to generated VSOURCE insertion, V6 showed the unsafe variants: T02 failed when the source used V5/resistor-style patched suffixes even with the 49-byte non-final source wire, and T04 failed when the manual source block was placed after the R/C/L body. Workspace files and user feedback indicate T00, T01, T03, T05, and T06 opened. Therefore DC-voltage source insertion should be source-first, should preserve standalone/manual source terminal/component suffix bytes, and should keep the second source wire in the 49-byte non-final form before the generated R/C/L source-net body.

rules.title: DC voltage source 6/21 confirmation uses source-first only
rules.rule: V7 applies only the V6 accepted source-first family to requested source-driven mixed R/C/L circuits. User testing confirmed all V7 cases worked: the 6-component DC-voltage source-driven circuit, the corrected 21-rule source-driven circuit using the standalone source block, and the manual source-block fallback. Source-driven DC-voltage circuits therefore use source nets DV/D0, no $TERPOWER records, no $TERGROUND records, no V0/G0 terminal labels, source-first ROOT.CDB order, and source global ID equal to the next component ID after the R/C/L specs.

rules.title: DC current source uses DI/I0 source-net convention
rules.rule: The user-created DC-current donors show a CSOURCE with an ordinary output terminal labelled DI and an ordinary input terminal labelled I0; I1/I4 are source references, not nets. The DI/I0 source-net convention remains valid evidence, but V8's current-source implementation is rejected: all DC-current generated topology cases failed while all DC-voltage cases worked. Do not use the standalone dc_current_01_default source block with ref I1/value 1A as the final current-source insertion method.

rules.title: DC current source connected-load donor is the active diagnostic direction
rules.rule: The user-made dc_current_03_resistor_load donor uses a connected CSOURCE record with visible ref I4, value 500mA, a 347-byte source record, source object before the resistor load, and a CDB where passive component records precede the current-source record. V9 proved that copying only the connected source block before generated R/C/L is not sufficient: T03 and onward failed with ISIS/VG dll errors. Do not use the source block alone as the final current-source method.

rules.title: DC current source may require donor DI/I0 anchor terminals
rules.rule: The connected current-load donor places a load-side DI $TERINPUT and I0 $TEROUTPUT immediately after the CSOURCE block and before the resistor component. V10 preserved this donor anchor terminal pair, chunk[655:858], after the connected source block, chunk[1:655]. User feedback rejected T02/T03/T04 mixed R/C/L anchor cases with ISIS dll errors, while T00/T01 were not reported as failing. V10 mixed cases used a combined device table with duplicate RESISTOR entries, so the anchor pair alone is not sufficient when device metadata is not DCV-style clean.

rules.title: DC current mixed cases should mirror DCV clean device table
rules.rule: Accepted DC-voltage mixed source cases use one clean device table with CAP, REALIND, RESISTOR, and VSOURCE. V10 mixed current cases instead had CAP, REALIND, RESISTOR, CSOURCE, and a second RESISTOR entry due combining the R/C/L donor table with the connected current-load donor table. V11 fixed the duplicate metadata by producing CAP + REALIND + RESISTOR + CSOURCE, but user feedback reported all V11 cases still gave ISIS dll errors. Therefore clean device metadata alone is not sufficient when the source geometry remains from the DI/I0 current-source donor family.

rules.title: Manual DC current source uses DCV geometry with CSOURCE metadata
rules.rule: The new user-supplied testing.pdsprj for DC current uses the same source net labels as DC voltage: DV for the positive/source side and D0 for the negative side. Its source reference/value are V1/10V, its visible source subckt text remains VSOURCE, but its final object model marker, ROOT.CDB model entry, and device-table model are CSOURCE. Its device table order is CAP, CSOURCE, REALIND, RESISTOR. User testing confirmed all V12 cases worked, including exact manual controls and generated R/C/L candidates that reused accepted DCV source geometry patched only at the final model marker to CSOURCE.

rules.title: DC current 15-topology pack applies V12 source method
rules.rule: For broad DC-current source topology generation, map the locked V0/G0 mixed R/C/L topology body to ordinary DV/D0 source nets, remove $TERPOWER/$TERGROUND and V0/G0 terminal labels, insert the accepted source-first DCV geometry patched to CSOURCE metadata, keep source ref/value V1/10V, and use a clean device table with CAP, CSOURCE, REALIND, and RESISTOR. User testing confirmed all 15 V13 DC-current source-driven topology cases worked.

rules.title: DC source-driven RCL generation is locked for current scope
rules.rule: For source-driven DC mixed R/C/L circuits, do not emit default V0 power terminals or G0 ground terminals unless a later explicit user request requires a separate power/ground symbol. DC voltage uses the accepted source-first VSOURCE method with ordinary DV/D0 source-net terminals. DC current uses the same accepted source-first source geometry and DV/D0 net labels, but its model identity is CSOURCE in the final object marker, ROOT.CDB, and device table. Both source types are confirmed across the requested 15 topology set.

rules.title: AC voltage source donors use VSINE with AV/A0 terminals
rules.rule: The supplied AC-voltage donors use ordinary two-character source-net labels AV and A0 and no $TERPOWER/$TERGROUND records in the source object chunk. The source model is VSINE, not VSOURCE. In ROOT.CDB, the source ref is V1, both the value field and model field are VSINE, and amplitude/frequency are property text fields such as {VA=20v} and {FREQ=5000hz}. V1 proved exact donor controls, E001 transplants, and generated AV/A0 R/C/L with no source work, but rejected generated source insertion from T05 onward with VGDVC.dll. Do not reuse V1's final standalone source block as a non-final generated source unit.

rules.title: AC voltage V2 tests exact non-final two-source VSINE unit
rules.rule: The two-source AC-voltage donor shows the first non-final AV/A0 VSINE unit is 673 bytes: output AV, input A0, V1 VSINE record, and two non-final 50-byte wire records. V2 user testing confirmed all generated cases worked, including simple, six-component, and corrected 21-rule R/C/L candidates using the exact non-final source unit. AC voltage source generation should therefore use source-first non-final donor source units rather than reusing a final standalone source block shape.

rules.title: Multiple DC sources use donor-spaced source-first units
rules.rule: V1 prepended donor-spaced source units before the accepted R/C/L source-net body, but all requested multi-source cases failed with ISIS.dll. V2 changed only source CDB rows to donor-style +/- pin names and also failed. Therefore the failure is not solved by source CDB pin maps alone; do not reuse V1/V2's combination of I-style current refs, concatenated device metadata, and mixed source rows.

rules.title: Generated source CDB rows do not blindly use donor +/- maps
evidence: accepted generated V7/V13 ROOT.CDB byte checks
rules.rule: Manual source donors can contain +/- pin names in ROOT.CDB, but the accepted generated DC-voltage and DC-current source-driven R/C/L packs use passive-style source row maps and work. V2 proved that forcing +/- source rows does not fix mixed multi-source ISIS.dll failures. Treat +/- as donor-specific evidence, not a universal generated-source rule.

rules.title: Mixed DC source V4 tests V-style refs and clean device metadata
rules.rule: V4 used archived four-source DCV units for unique source suffixes, V-style refs, accepted generated passive CDB maps, CSOURCE final model identity for current sources, and a clean ordered device section. User testing reported all V4 cases failed with ISIS.dll, including source-only controls. Therefore V-style refs plus clean device ordering are not sufficient, and the immediate failure is in mixed source object/device handling or long path/name handling, before R/C/L topology matters.

rules.title: MX5 short-name mixed source diagnostics isolate path and source metadata
rules.rule: MX5 wrote short-name controls A0/A1/B0/B1/B2/C1-C5, but the user then supplied an all-source donor containing VSOURCE, CSOURCE, and VSINE. MX6 supersedes MX5 as the preferred next test because it uses that donor's combined source-family metadata.

rules.title: All-source donor supplies combined source-family metadata
rules.rule: The user-supplied 45454New Project.pdsprj contains VSOURCE, CSOURCE, and VSINE source-family metadata in one project. D0 exact copy and D1 E001 transplant worked, proving its object chunk/CDB/device metadata are packer-safe. MX6 E0/E1 failed with bad object record because they still used old 4x-DCV source-unit records. Therefore mixed source generation must use the all-source donor's own source object records, not just its device table.

rules.title: V7 tests all-source donor VSOURCE/CSOURCE object records
rules.rule: V7 duplicated the all-source donor's own VSOURCE and CSOURCE records directly. User feedback indicates T00-T03 worked, so donor copy/transplant and duplicated source-only VSOURCE/CSOURCE records are safe. T04 onward failed with ISIS.dll, so the failure starts when generated R/C/L records are added through the synthetic all-source+R/C/L join. Do not treat source CDB pin maps as the primary failure after V7; investigate device-section composition and source/RCL join ordering.

rules.title: Mixed DC source device sections should be spliced by entry, not concatenated whole
rules.rule: Accepted single-source DCV and DCI packs used coherent donor device sections that already contained their source family plus R/C/L devices. V7 failed only after combining all-source metadata with R/C/L metadata for requested circuits. V8 tested entry-level CSOURCE device splicing, but the later user-supplied mixed source plus R/C/L donor provides a stronger complete-source/RCL ordering authority, so V8 is superseded as the next decision point.

rules.title: Mixed DC source plus RCL donor uses source-tail object order
rules.rule: The working mixed source plus corrected 21-component R/C/L donor keeps the R/C/L body first and appends the VSOURCE/CSOURCE source records at the tail. It removes actual $TERPOWER/$TERGROUND bridge objects from the object chunk but keeps the leading ordinary $TEROUTPUT V0 terminal. Its coherent device section order is CAP, CSOURCE, REALIND, RESISTOR, VSOURCE. Its ROOT.CDB rows are passives first, then I1 CSOURCE, then V1 VSOURCE. V9 user testing confirmed donor copy/transplant and terminal label mutation work, but generated-body replacement fails from T03 onward with VGDVC.dll. Do not replace the full donor body for mixed-source R/C/L until final-unit/order mutations are isolated.

rules.title: Mixed DC source generated body failure starts at final RL ordering
rules.rule: V9 T03 shares the donor source tail byte-for-byte, so the VGDVC.dll failure is in the generated R/C/L body, not in the appended source tail. Byte comparison shows a semantic mismatch in the final RL group. V10 proved generated CDB rows are safe on donor object streams because T03 and T04 worked, but generated-prefix splices still failed. T05/T06 gave VGDVC.dll, and T07/T08 produced a missing-library/crash path. The V10 splice started too late at OUT A9 offset 13019; the complete donor final RL group starts at IN A9 offset 12813 and includes the preceding group input/output terminal records. Do not splice mid-group.

rules.title: Mixed DC source diagnostics must splice whole donor RCL groups
rules.rule: Generated-prefix splice cases must cut only at whole donor group boundaries and must remap generated prefix terminal/link suffix bytes to the donor suffix scheme before joining to donor suffix records. V11 T03 and T05, the suffix-map variants, opened; T02, T04, T06, and T07 all gave VGDVC.dll. Plain group-boundary splicing is therefore not enough. Avoid variable-length DVO-to-D0 label shrinking on generated splice cases unless separately proven, because V10 T07/T08 showed that shrink-patched generated splices can corrupt device identity into a missing-library dialog.

rules.title: Mixed DC source visual relocation must preserve source suffix bytes
rules.rule: V11 suffix-map cases opened but the source blocks were visually too far from their connected terminal labels. V12 relocated donor source sub-blocks by patching only terminal symbol/label coordinates, WIRE coordinates, and source component coordinate fields while preserving record lengths and terminal/link suffix bytes. User testing reported all V12 cases opened, confirming source relocation is safe, but the leading V0 terminal remained away from the source and a long line crossed the sheet.

rules.title: Mixed RCL negative-row nonfinal wire high byte must be repaired
rules.rule: Some generated non-final WIRE records in lower rows contain a negative y2 coordinate whose high byte has been overwritten to 00, producing y2-y1 = 0x01000000 and a sheet-crossing visual line. V13 repairs those wire y2 fields after suffix mapping and before source/V0 coordinate relocation. It also moves the leading ordinary OUT V0 terminal beside the VSOURCE upper wire point while preserving suffix bytes. User feedback confirmed the V13 outputs open and the visuals are good enough for this stage.

rules.title: Requested mixed DC-source circuits duplicate V13 source units
rules.rule: For complex mixed DC voltage/current source R/C/L circuits, generate the passive R/C/L source-net body first, then append duplicated donor-derived VSOURCE/CSOURCE units using V13-safe coordinate relocation, source-local positive terminals, repaired generated WIRE high bytes, unique source global IDs, source values patched in both ROOT.DSN visible value records and ROOT.CDB rows, and passives-first/source-last ROOT.CDB ordering. User testing confirmed all five requested V14 circuits and the clean post-V9 V15 rerun worked, so this method is locked for the current multi-source DC scope.

rules.title: DC-voltage RCL topology pack uses source-first VSOURCE plus V13 wire repair
rules.rule: For the 15 locked mixed R/C/L topology examples driven by one DC voltage source, use the accepted V8 source-first standalone VSOURCE block with DV as the positive source net and D0 as the negative source net, emit no $TERPOWER/$TERGROUND or V0/G0 labels, and apply the V13 negative-row WIRE high-byte repair before packing.

rules.title: Source-driven single and two-family passive probes reuse accepted source families
rules.rule: Source-driven generation is not limited to full R/C/L loads. User testing confirmed SOURCE_PASSIVE_V1 worked for R-only, C-only, L-only, RC, RL, and LC loads across DC voltage, DC current, and AC voltage. Continue using the accepted source-family methods: DCV V15 source-first VSOURCE plus V13 WIRE repair, DCI V13 DCV-geometry patched to CSOURCE identity plus V13 WIRE repair, and ACV V2 exact non-final AV/A0 VSINE unit.

rules.title: Two-source passive probes use V14 DC source duplication and duplicated ACV V2 units
rules.rule: SOURCE_PASSIVE_V2 tested source multiplicity after V1 proved single-source passive loads. User feedback confirmed the V2 cases worked except the pure two-DC-voltage-source cases SRCP_V2_DCV2_T01_R_ONLY and SRCP_V2_DCV2_T02_RC_RL, which gave a bad object record, opened visibly correct, then failed simulation with SPICE singular #V2#branch. Therefore do not lock pure DCV+DCV source-driven passive loads with only a common D0 return. DC current two-source, mixed DC voltage/current, and AC voltage two-source passive loads remain provisionally accepted from this batch.

rules.title: Generated V3 DCV2 grounded-return order is rejected
rules.rule: SOURCE_PASSIVE_V3 generated pure DCV+DCV grounded-return cases by splitting source output terminals to the front of the object stream and using generated passive-style source CDB rows. User testing reported every generated V3 case gave bad object record. A later user-fixed V3 T03 file still contains the D0-to-G0 high-value reference, so $TERGROUND alone is not the proven cause. Do not reuse generated V3's split-output source ordering or passive-style source CDB rows.

rules.title: Pure DCV2 passive loads should mirror manual two-source donor returns
rules.rule: The manual two-DC-voltage-source donor contains no $TERPOWER or $TERGROUND records and uses two ordinary source-net terminal pairs, but SOURCE_PASSIVE_V4 reported VGDVC errors when adapted for source-driven passive loads. Do not continue the V4 manual-2x-source route until a smaller donor-preserving diagnostic proves which byte range is safe.

rules.title: Pure DCV2 passive fallback uses fixed V3 component-first source units
rules.rule: The user-fixed V3 T03 file uses passive R/C/L groups first, then component-first VSOURCE units ordered as VSOURCE, output terminal, wire, input terminal, wire, but generated SOURCE_PASSIVE_V5 cases using that reconstructed order gave VGDVC.dll. User clarified generated V3 at least opened and rendered correctly. Do not replace the generated V3 ROOT.DSN object stream with reconstructed fixed-order source units.

rules.title: Pure DCV2 passive debugging preserves V3 DSN and tests CDB only
rules.rule: SOURCE_PASSIVE_V6 preserved generated V3 ROOT.DSN byte-for-byte and tested CDB variants, including exact user-fixed CDB and source-style +/1 -/2 rows, but user testing reported all V6 cases gave bad object record. Therefore CDB-only mutation over generated V3 ROOT.DSN is rejected for pure DCV+DCV source-driven passive repair.

rules.title: Pure DCV2 passive controls must prove fixed-file copy and repack first
rules.rule: The user-fixed V3 T03 file is a valid pure DCV+DCV passive oracle. User testing confirmed exact copying, deterministic deflated repacking, ZIP_STORED repacking, E001 ROOT.DSN/ROOT.CDB transplant, and ROOT.CDB-only source value mutation from 1V/1V to 10V/5V all work. Packer/container context is not the cause of the prior bad-object failures.

rules.title: Pure DCV2 passive scale-up must isolate source visible values and compact passive suffixes
rules.rule: SOURCE_PASSIVE_V8 proved the fixed-file controls remain safe but generated passive body rebuilds still fail: user feedback reported T02 and onward gave VGDVC.dll. Exact resistor visible strings and compact fixed-oracle suffixes are not sufficient. Do not reuse V8's generated passive-body path for pure DCV+DCV passive scale-up.

rules.title: Pure DCV2 passive rebuild must preserve resistor wire endpoints and source-boundary bytes
rules.rule: Byte comparison after V8 found two concrete generated ROOT.DSN defects: resistor left-wire records collapsed to the terminal coordinate instead of running from terminal to resistor body, and non-final source input-wire bytes were overwritten at the passive/source boundary. SOURCE_PASSIVE_V9 fixes resistor wire endpoints, preserves non-final source wire bytes, and trims the passive-source boundary by two bytes. User testing confirmed all V9 cases worked, including byte-exact R-only oracle rebuild, R-only 10V/5V mutation, and RC/RL scale-up variants.

rules.title: Source-driven RCL generation is promoted to the production CLI
rules.rule: Use src/proteusgen/source_driven.py and the generate-source-driven CLI for source-driven circuits. DC voltage/current generation uses the accepted V15 donor-derived source units, ordinary two-character source-net terminals, source-local placement, unique global IDs, and V13 negative-wire high-byte repair. One AC voltage source uses the accepted V2 exact non-final VSINE unit. Passive groups use the locked mixed-RCL whole-group renderer. AC current remains unsupported. A circuit without a requested source must continue through the passive generator; source defaulting is a planner rule, not a generator mutation.

rules.title: Topology-aware V2 beautifier is the production layout default
rules.rule: Use the exact accepted V2 deterministic layout algorithm before binary emission. Omitted layout defaults to beautify, explicit component or source positions without a strategy infer manual, and explicit legacy remains available. Keep donor-derived component, terminal, source, and short-wire records together; do not synthesize standalone routed wires or junctions. Preserve double-source clearance, compact AC-source geometry, repeated-node lane preference, object identities, CDB ordering, and electrical labels.

rules.title: Bidirectional endpoints require role-based orientation and source-native DCV records
rules.rule: Build $TERBIDIR records from the exact orientation donors. Convert ordinary output-role endpoints to angle 0 and ordinary input-role endpoints to angle 1800; do not preserve the legacy numeric angle blindly. For DC voltage sources, use a complete donor-native bidirectional terminal/source/wire unit, activate each terminal suffix and matching source-body suffix together, and encode the ROOT.CDB pin map as +->1 and -->2. V3 is the production default across all passive and supported source routes after all eleven broad regression cases passed manual Proteus testing.

rules.title: Beautified production output uses the compact post-V3 component grid
rules.rule: Use 3175000 horizontal and 2032000 vertical Proteus units for automatic component placement. Preserve the accepted 5080000 multi-source vertical clearance, same-name node preference, seven-slot wrapping, deterministic ordering, and zero-overlap validation.

rules.title: IC generation starts from ordinary-terminal donor learning
rules.rule: For the IC phase, do not emit DC voltage, DC current, AC voltage, or AC current source components. Treat combinational 74-series IC supply as hidden unless a donor proves otherwise. Use ordinary input and output terminals on IC signal pins. In mixed IC/passive circuits, R/C/L endpoints use the accepted donor-derived bidirectional terminal method, and power/ground terminals keep their accepted special terminal handling for logic constants or passive references. The V1 donor-learning pack passed user Proteus testing for exact donor repack, E001 transplant, label-only mutation, two-package scaling control, power/ground logic constants, diagnostic RCL-load transplant, and HC32 cross-family controls. The real HC08 five-circuit pack also passed user Proteus testing, so production-style HC08 composition is accepted for the tested gate/passive shapes while expression-driven multi-package output remains pending manual Proteus testing.

rules.title: 74HC08 user DIP pins normalize to Proteus gate subparts
rules.rule: When a user describes a 74HC08 as a 14-pin DIP package, ignore pin 14/VCC/+5V and pin 7/GND/0V as hidden IC supply connections. Do not emit U1 pin-14 or pin-7 connections. Map signal pins to the accepted Proteus subparts: pins 1/2/3 are U1:A IN1/IN2/OUT, pins 4/5/6 are U1:B IN1/IN2/OUT, pins 9/10/8 are U1:C IN1/IN2/OUT, and pins 12/13/11 are U1:D IN1/IN2/OUT. Power and ground terminals remain allowed only for logic constants or passive ground/supply nodes. Fail closed on unsupported pins rather than silently dropping them.

rules.title: 74HC08 Boolean expression synthesis starts with AND-only reductions
rules.rule: The first Boolean expression interpreter supports AND-only assignments. Accept symbols such as AND, *, &, &&, middle-dot, and LaTeX \cdot as AND operators; reject OR, XOR, NOT, +, |, !, and unsupported operators. Normalize variables such as X_1 and X_{10}, compact temporary Proteus labels X10..X15 to XA..XF, reduce the expression through deterministic two-input AND tree levels, and allocate gates in package order U1:A, U1:B, U1:C, U1:D, U2:A, and onward. Ignore pin 14 and pin 7 as hidden package supply for every 74HC08 package. The 15-input, four-package HC08 AND expression pack passed manual Proteus testing.

rules.title: 74HC32 Boolean expression synthesis starts with OR-only reductions
rules.rule: The OR expression interpreter accepts OR, +, |, and || operators and rejects AND, XOR, NOT, and mixed operators. It uses the same deterministic two-input reduction shape as the accepted HC08 AND path, but emits donor-derived 74HC32/74OR2 component-first gate records from IC_HC32_M02_ALL4_IO. HC32 gate record ids and pin-link ids are 32-bit unaligned fields and must be patched separately from the older HC08 16-bit suffix method. The first generated test maps a 15-input OR expression across U1:A-D, U2:A-D, U3:A-D, and U4:A-B; user testing confirmed it worked in Proteus.

rules.title: Mixed 74HC08 and 74HC32 with RCL starts with a 15-gate diagnostic
rules.rule: The first mixed AND/OR/RCL diagnostic intentionally emitted exactly fifteen IC gate subparts, not a fourteen-gate pure reduction tree. It used eight 74HC08 AND2 gates to create A1..A8, seven 74HC32 OR2 gates to reduce those nodes to Y0, then routed Y0 through a resistor, capacitor, and inductor branch to G0. Although static validation was clean, user Proteus testing reported an ISIS.dll violation. Do not promote this V1 method. The later donor tests indicate the old merged device section was unsafe for this mixed shape; do not treat same-name input/output/bidirectional labels as the rejected part without separate evidence.

rules.title: All-bidirectional IC signal terminals are diagnostic only
rules.rule: The user-supplied mixed manual donor uses bidirectional terminals for all visible signal and passive connection points, plus special power/ground records, and places passive/terminal/wire records before bare IC component bodies. The V2 generated diagnostic using the manual donor device section and all-bidirectional visible terminals opened successfully in Proteus, proving the donor/device-section path is useful. However, it is not production policy: IC signal pins must preserve electrical direction with $TERINPUT for inputs and $TEROUTPUT for outputs, because an IC input pin must not be represented as an output-capable bidirectional terminal.

rules.title: Mixed IC and passive circuits preserve IC terminal direction
rules.rule: For mixed IC/passive circuits, keep IC signal pins directional: IC inputs are $TERINPUT and IC outputs are $TEROUTPUT. R/C/L and other passive endpoints use the accepted $TERBIDIR method. Same-name $TERINPUT, $TEROUTPUT, and $TERBIDIR labels connect in Proteus. Use the working manual donor device-section path for mixed 74HC08/74HC32/RCL shapes. The corrected V3 diagnostic with 30 IC input terminals, 15 IC output terminals, and 6 bidirectional passive terminals passed manual Proteus testing.

rules.title: Remaining quad combinational IC donors are staged for acceptance
rules.rule: The remaining combinational donor corpus is imported, statically analyzed, and manually accepted. The first V1 test pack used E001 transplants and label-only mutation, not expression synthesis. 74HC00 uses a terminal-first gate record family similar to HC08. 74HC02, 74HC86, and 74HC266 use component-first gate records similar to HC32. The 74HC266 donor is treated as the XNOR candidate but must preserve its observed Proteus 74XOR2 function marker until a generated semantic XNOR test proves the exact behavior.

rules.title: Remaining combinational generated logic starts with compact one-package tests
rules.rule: After donor acceptance, the first generated-object pack for 74HC00, 74HC02, 74HC86, and 74HC266 must stay compact: one package and three generated gate subparts per family. It tests NAND3, NOR3, XOR4, and a 74HC266 XNOR-chain diagnostic using accepted all-four donor gate slices. Preserve the observed 74HC266 74XOR2 function marker until Proteus behavior confirms the semantic mapping. Larger multi-package expression synthesis should wait for this generated pack to pass manual Proteus testing.

rules.title: Final combinational IC acceptance pack uses six accepted gate families
rules.rule: The final combinational IC V1 acceptance pack maps the user's 30 circuit blueprints onto accepted donor-derived gate slices for 74HC08 AND, 74HC32 OR, 74HC00 NAND, 74HC02 NOR, 74HC86 XOR, and 74HC266 XNOR-candidate gates. IC package supply instructions for pin 14 and pin 7 are treated as user-input metadata only; no explicit IC supply pins are emitted. IC signal pins remain $TERINPUT/$TEROUTPUT, while R/C/L endpoints use the accepted $TERBIDIR method with special V0/G0 terminals when passive branches need them. The prompt's 74HC7266 name is normalized to 74HC266. Circuit 30 is included as an AND-output plus relay/snubber interface only because no MOSFET donor has been accepted. The user reported the full 30-pack worked, then requested a targeted compact-layout and bidirectional-G0 refinement for the final two mixed IC/passive cases before final lock-in.

rules.title: Final IC last-two refinement tests compact layout and bidirectional passive G0
rules.rule: The targeted V2 final-last-two pack kept IC signal pins directional and converted passive G0 endpoints from donor $TERGROUND records into same-name $TERBIDIR records. User testing reported that T29 failed while T30 worked; T30 did not exercise a passive G0 endpoint. Do not promote passive G0 as $TERBIDIR for mixed IC/passive T29-style circuits. The compact layout portion remains reusable only after retesting with the previous donor $TERGROUND method.

rules.title: Compact T29 retest restores donor ground method
rules.rule: The corrected V3 T29 retest keeps compact small-circuit placement but restores passive G0 to the previous donor $TERGROUND method. IC signal pins remain $TERINPUT/$TEROUTPUT and ordinary R/C/L endpoints remain $TERBIDIR. User testing reported this V3 T29 output worked, so compact small mixed-IC placement is accepted only with passive G0 kept as donor $TERGROUND.

rules.title: 74HC04 NOT generation uses unary 74INV subparts
rules.rule: The HC04 donor shows hex inverter subparts U1:A through U1:F using the 74INV.MDF model. Each subpart has one signal input and one signal output; user DIP pin 14/VCC and pin 7/GND are hidden-supply metadata and must not be emitted as explicit IC package pins. The HC04 donor's visible input terminal labels are one character, so HC04 generation uses a dedicated resizable terminal-label patch plus HC04-specific suffix and coordinate handling. User testing confirmed the HC04/all-seven pack works. Production IC generation now accepts the locked gate/passive JSON route, keeps IC signal pins as $TERINPUT/$TEROUTPUT, keeps ordinary passive endpoints as $TERBIDIR, and keeps passive G0 on the donor $TERGROUND method.

rules.title: Sequential IC solo donor packs use bidirectional visible pins
rules.rule: For the accepted sequential IC solo donor packs, preserve donor-native $TERBIDIR records for all visible IC pins. The accepted scope is exact repack, E001 transplant, label mutation, same-family 2x/4x controls where donors exist, and RLC donor transplants in the generated folders. Do not apply this policy to locked combinational ICs, whose pins remain directional. Do not infer that mixed sequential IC synthesis works; unit slicing and same-length identity mutation were rejected earlier. The user-facing 74HC47 donor uses Proteus marker 7447, and the supplied 74HC174 donors remain distinct from the still-missing 74HC175.

rules.title: Analog and misc solo donor pack preserves whole donor chunks
rules.rule: For the accepted analog/misc solo donor pack, preserve whole donor chunks and donor-native $TERBIDIR endpoints. The accepted scope is exact repack, E001 transplant, label mutation, same-family scale controls where donors exist, and whole RLC donor transplants. ELEC-CAP uses the Proteus marker CAP-ELEC and its original donor terminal labels are blank, so generated labels must be patched from that observed shape. Do not promote mixed-family analog synthesis from this evidence alone.

rules.title: Real mixed IC/analog donors support whole-chunk relabeling
rules.rule: The six real mixed IC/analog donor projects can be exact-repacked, transplanted into E001 with the donor ROOT.CDB and device section, and topology-preserving relabeled while retaining donor-native $TERBIDIR visible endpoints. This accepted evidence covers complete donor chunks only. It does not authorize arbitrary unit slicing, same-length identity mutation, or subset removal; those remain separate experiments. Initial region analysis shows the analog/RCL prefix must be treated as one balanced bundle, and 74HC193 plus 74HC192 must be kept together because their individual terminal/WIRE counts are not balanced.

rules.title: Mixed IC/analog subset removal preserves complete balanced regions
rules.rule: Complete contiguous object-region removal works for the accepted real mixed donor corpus when the full donor ROOT.CDB and donor device section are preserved. Keep the analog/RCL prefix as one balanced bundle, and keep the 74HC193 plus 74HC192 pair together unless a later donor proves independent safe rows. Individually balanced regions such as 4017, 4020, 74HC4024, later counter/divider ICs, 74HC595, 74HC165, 74HC157, 74HC283, and 74HC85 may be retained or removed as complete regions. This does not yet prove cross-donor merging or metadata cleanup.

rules.title: Cross-donor IC metadata cannot concatenate unpatched device sections
rules.rule: Do not concatenate complete donor device sections without patching every embedded object-data tail pointer. V1 cross-donor cases used clean whole IC regions and union CDB rows, but T01/T06 produced LXLCORE.dll errors and T02-T05 crashed Proteus before opening. The likely rejected part is the metadata merge: each extracted donor device section ends with an object-data pointer, and V1 patched only the final concatenated section tail via the old single-section builder. Cross-donor retry must patch every section tail pointer and keep CDB rows ordered by numeric U reference before any further conclusions about visible region mixing are drawn.

rules.title: Cross-donor whole device-section merge remains unsafe after pointer patching
rules.rule: Do not merge cross-donor IC metadata by concatenating whole donor device sections, even if every section tail pointer is patched and CDB rows are sorted by numeric U reference. V2 reproduced the V1 failure pattern: T01/T06 gave LXLCORE.dll errors and T02-T05 crashed while opening. Device-section analysis shows donor sections are sequences of length-prefixed per-device definitions followed by one final pointer footer. Whole-section merges leave unwanted duplicate/trailing definitions and section-level structure in the merged metadata. The next safe probe must extract only required per-device definitions, omit donor section footers, and emit exactly one generated footer.

rules.title: Cross-donor static validation must verify visible object refs are covered by ROOT.CDB refs
rules.rule: For generated cross-donor IC projects, extract every visible U-reference from the ROOT.DSN object chunk and verify it is present in ROOT.CDB before manual Proteus testing. The previous V1/V2/V3 checks missed 74HC157 fragments whose object chunk contained U50 while the selected CDB row was U5.
rules.rationale: User testing showed identical V1/V2/V3 failures. A later byte audit found T01/T03/T05/T06 were invalid before Proteus because object refs were not a subset of CDB refs.

rules.title: Cross-donor mixed ICs require full donor device sections, not filtered per-device metadata
rules.rule: For cross-donor mixed IC experiments using the sequential/misc IC families, preserve the complete device section from every donor family involved. Do not use filtered per-device definitions for this route until a Proteus-authored mixed donor proves a smaller safe model.
rules.rationale: Isolation V1 user testing showed T02 worked when full multi-donor device sections were present. T03 crashed when foreign device metadata was absent, and T04 onward crashed with filtered device definitions or generated CDB/device combinations.

rules.title: Do not ASCII-slice ROOT.CDB rows
rules.rule: For CDB synthesis, parse binary row boundaries and rebuild through src/proteusgen/cdb.py. Do not split ROOT.CDB rows at ASCII U-reference markers or concatenate rows without adapting property-row overlap/trailer bytes.
rules.rationale: Isolation V2 user testing showed every old generated/stitched CDB case crashed before opening. The later byte-level decoder proved those rows had been sliced at invalid boundaries and missed the property-row overlap rule.

rules.title: Do not reduce ROOT.CDB skeletons for cross-donor ICs
rules.rule: For cross-donor sequential/misc IC CDB experiments, do not emit a reduced CDB count with only visible/generated rows. Preserve a complete donor CDB skeleton until full-skeleton replacement testing proves a smaller safe model.
rules.rationale: CDB V1 used parser-built row boundaries, property-row overlap adaptation, and both original and renumbered ordinals, but user testing reported only the full-CDB controls T00 and T06 worked. Every reduced generated-CDB case crashed before opening.

rules.title: Use full CDB skeleton replacement for cross-donor ICs
rules.rule: For cross-donor sequential/misc IC mixtures, preserve full donor device sections and a complete donor ROOT.CDB skeleton. Use the parser-built CDB row replacement path inside that full skeleton; do not reduce the CDB skeleton/count.
rules.rationale: CDB V2 user testing showed full-skeleton replacement worked for all cases except a non-crashing T05 DLL error. The focused CDB V3 T05 isolation then reported all cases worked, including U2, U3, U2+U3, property-only, and pin-only replacements.

rules.title: Do not silently remove visible 74HC4060 U9 from mixed IC work
rules.rule: Do not silently drop visible 74HC4060/U9 from practical mixed sequential/misc IC work. If a broad generated pack cannot yet make visible 74HC4060 simulate, stop and generate focused 74HC4060 diagnostics with accepted solo/RLC and mixed analog/RLC donor contexts. Only mark 74HC4060 unsupported for a route after those focused controls prove the failing boundary.
rules.rationale: User testing of the accepted V1 practical pack produced no-model simulation errors for U9 in both T03 and T08. V2 then removed visible 74HC4060, but the user rejected that direction because the generator must learn how to support the component rather than hiding it.

rules.title: IC region translation must move terminal labels and component text
rules.rule: When translating a complete donor-derived IC region, move $TERBIDIR terminal symbol coordinates, $TERBIDIR terminal-label coordinates, WIRE endpoints, component ID/value/subckt/properties text coordinates, and the IC body anchor together. Do not translate only the body and pin symbols.
rules.rationale: V2 moved IC bodies and terminal symbols but left terminal labels and component text at old donor coordinates, producing visible floating artifacts in every generated case even when simulation passed.

rules.title: Do not use heuristic coordinate scanning for mixed sequential IC layout
rules.rule: Do not translate mixed sequential IC regions by scanning every integer pair that looks like an x/y coordinate. Only patch coordinate fields that are known from record structure, or keep accepted no-layout whole-region placement until a precise parser is available.
rules.rationale: MIXED_IC_FOCUSED_V3_TEMP_2026_06_10 used a broad coordinate scan after V2 artifacts. User testing reported T01/T02 did not work, so V4 removes this scan and returns T01/T02 to accepted no-layout baselines.

rules.title: 74HC4060 no-model errors require DSN and CDB model-property testing
rules.rule: Do not add VOLTAGE=4.5V to 74HC4060 instance metadata. The V4 DSN/CDB property patch that combined MODFILE and VOLTAGE caused netlist linker VALUE+VOLTAGE mapping errors.
rules.rationale: User testing of V4 reported T05/T06/T07 failed. Screenshots showed VALUE+VOLTAGE not found in the parameter mapping table for 74HC4060+4.5V, so the patch created a different failure instead of solving the no-model boundary.

rules.title: Use refreshed 74HC4060 donors; legacy repo 4060 is rejected
rules.rule: Do not use the legacy repo 74HC4060 donor set for future generation. User testing rejected old exact-rezip T018 and accepted refreshed 4060 exact-rezip cases T034 onward. Canonical sequential_ics_batch3 4060 donors are replaced with the refreshed donor files; legacy files are retained only under sequential_ics_4060_legacy_bad_20260610 for negative evidence. Mutation and pairwise mixing with refreshed 4060 still require their own Proteus tests.
rules.rationale: The earlier no-model finding was based on stale/corrupt 4060 donor evidence. The exact-rezip boundary test separated donor validity from generator mutation and showed the refreshed donor set is the active baseline.

rules.title: Analog/basic donor-native label edits open and simulate; topology intent still requires Proteus-visible validation
rules.rule: Mixed analog/basic donor-native projects containing RLC, NPN, PNP, LM741, and CAP-ELEC can open and simulate when donor-native metadata is preserved and terminal labels are edited. However, V6 showed that a generated same-name topology edit may still not match the intended visible/electrical terminal naming in Proteus, so do not claim functional topology correctness from terminal_plan alone.

rules.title: NE555 donor-native label edits open and simulate; output-to-load intent still requires Proteus-visible validation
rules.rule: NE555 donor-native projects with an existing RLC donor load can open and simulate when donor-native metadata is preserved and terminal labels are edited. V6 showed that same-name output-to-load edits are not accepted from generated terminal_plan evidence alone; verify the actual Proteus-visible terminal names/electrical grouping before promoting NE555 functional topology generation.

rules.title: Exact donor-content rezip is the next IC model boundary test
rules.rule: Before further IC topology mutation, test exact donor-content rezips for every currently supplied IC family. Exact rezip outputs must preserve every internal ZIP member payload byte-for-byte. A failure in this pack is a donor/model/Proteus-install boundary, not a generator mutation bug.

rules.title: Old 74HC4520 exact rezip is rejected; refreshed 4520 donors need exact-rezip proof
rules.rule: Do not use old T020 74HC4520 donor evidence as a valid source. User testing rejected old exact-rezip T020. Use the refreshed 74HC4520 donor set only after T038-T041 exact-rezip probes pass in Proteus.

rules.title: IC pairwise V1 uses a 34-source IC-only exact-rezip matrix
rules.rule: Do not promote IC_PAIRWISE_34_V1. User testing found repeatable duplicate part reference failures across early combinational/sequential pairings, no-model failures involving 7447/74HC47 pairings, and refreshed 4060 coordinate artifacts. Use V2 or later for pairwise retesting.
evidence: User pasted V1 pairwise results on 2026-06-10

rules.title: Mixed IC pair CDB rows must be composed by package property refs
rules.rule: CDB property-row parsing/composition is necessary but not sufficient for pairwise IC support. Do not use IC_PAIRWISE_34_V2 as a promotion path. User testing reported that V2 repeated the old simulation errors for cases that opened and caused crashes in cases that previously only had simulation or coordinate issues. For combinational failed pairs, regenerate through the accepted combinational gate-slice writer instead of whole-donor U2 copying.
evidence: User V1 reports: duplicate part reference U2:A [U1:A] and duplicate X000000.. refs
P001_S01_S02 V2 focused check: pin refs U1:A/U2:A and property refs U1/U2

rules.title: Refreshed 4060 pairwise movement needs short body marker and component text coordinates
rules.rule: For refreshed 74HC4060 donors, do not use the V2 full pairwise regeneration path. User testing reported S32/S33/S34 crashed in V2 even though V1 only needed a coordinate cleanup. Revisit 4060 only as a minimal coordinate-only patch over the V1 artifact that already opened/simulated, and do not change CDB/device composition for those pairs.
evidence: User V1 reports: S32/S33/S34 simulated but terminals were far from pins with long weird wires
User V2 reports: S32/S33/S34 now crashed after the V2 regeneration
P033_S01_S34 V2 focused check: 4 body coordinate pairs and 12 component text coordinate pairs translated

rules.title: Failed combinational IC pairs must use accepted gate-slice generation, not whole-donor U2 copying
rules.rule: For pairwise failures involving already-accepted combinational IC families, do not concatenate exact-rezip donor chunks as left donor plus moved U2 donor. Use the accepted combinational generator for combinational sides: fresh gate record slices, fresh object/suffix IDs, directional IC terminals, and generated CDB subpart rows with package property rows. For mixed accepted-combinational plus exact-donor pairs, keep the non-combinational donor native and add the combinational gate with a fresh package ref and object ID after the donor. Do not apply this rule to non-combinational-only or coordinate-only failures.
evidence: User V1 report: S01+S02 opens but simulation fails with duplicate part reference U2:A [U1:A] and duplicate X000000.. refs
User reported IC_PAIRWISE_ERROR_FOCUSED_V1 T01_S01_S02 worked on 2026-06-10

rules.rule: The expanded pairwise error repair path is accepted for V1-rejected pairs that include an accepted combinational side. It generated only V1-rejected pairs with an accepted combinational side: 65 projects total, 15 pure accepted-combinational pairs and 50 accepted-combinational plus exact-donor pairs. It deliberately deferred 44 pairs: non-combinational-only failures and coordinate-only refreshed-4060 cases.
evidence: User reported focused S01+S02 repair worked
User reported all 65 IC_PAIRWISE_ERROR_FIXED_V2 projects worked on 2026-06-11

rules.title: All pairwise cases with accepted combinational ICs can be generated through the combinational-side method for testing
rules.rule: After IC_PAIRWISE_ERROR_FIXED_V2 passed user Proteus testing, the same method was expanded to every unordered pair containing S01..S07. Accepted combinational sides are regenerated from locked gate slices; non-combinational paired sides remain exact native donors. The 2026-06-11 pack generated 210 such cases with zero static validation issues, but user Proteus testing is still required before promotion.
evidence: User reported all 65 IC_PAIRWISE_ERROR_FIXED_V2 projects worked on 2026-06-11

rules.title: Non-combinational pairwise donor probes should patch CDB IDs only on collision
rules.rule: For non-combinational-only pair probes, preserve both exact donor chunks and patch the right donor package ref/terminal labels. Patch right-side CDB pin/property IDs only when they collide with left-side IDs; preserve native IDs when unique. This is not an accepted production rule until Proteus testing confirms the 21-probe pack.
evidence: P211_S08_S09_NONCOMB_FRESH_CDB_IDS_PROBE changes right CDB ID 1 to 2 because of collision
P471_S21_S22_NONCOMB_FRESH_CDB_IDS_PROBE preserves right IDs 33 and 23 because they do not collide
